title: I Spent a Week Making a Game about Vacuuming
beats: Confession of a streak of abandoned projects (fluids, dunes, audio, neural nets) before a one-week game
Rule: one week, then publish no matter what; ask GPT-3 for ideas, pick superhero doing chores
Vacuum from three cubes, hose from a path tool, hero as a cube
FABRIK: chain of bones, target; stretch the end to the target, fix lengths backward, then forward, repeat
Shows his code, admits it needs optimization, moves on; demo by dragging the target
Hose goes through the player; body follows reluctantly
Same algorithm on the power cable looks wrong; rejects it as not good enough
Verlet-style rope: Point (position, previous position, lock), Stick (keeps two points apart); build rope
Per-frame code: carry momentum, add gravity, store previous position; then stick constraints
Fixing one stick breaks a neighbour, so run constraints repeatedly until it settles
Test on a more complex setup, then cable with floor collision and unplug rule
Same Points and Sticks as a grid for cape cloth; cut sticks with mouse; randomize update order to kill jitter
Ships the engine's built-in cloth instead; says it was still fun
Dust: half a million instanced cubes, instance ID selects position from buffer
Purpose of instancing: remove draw-call overhead; same buffer can hold rotation, colour
Compute shader sucks in near particles, disables ones under nozzle, counter
Density weight map: sample random positions, keep the one with highest weight
Floorboards from random-length cubes, infinite-loop crashes, Blender furniture as physics objects
Ghosts reuse dust code as orbiting particles; sucking mechanic, suction lines, object pooling
Commissioned theme song via Fiverr, arrives at deadline; played in full
Admits game is fun for two minutes, over-scoped; buggy grocery-shopping prototype, quaternion bug

metrics.brute_force: yes 4:14: reused FABRIK on the cable and showed it failing before the better method; relaxation itself is iterate until stable (6:29)
metrics.examples: 3 constraint uses (hose, cable, cloth) then dust, ghosts; sizes grow tiny rope to cloth grid to 500k particles
metrics.ending: Personal reflection and joke song, no recap of techniques

principles.2: partly: Point and Stick are introduced one at a time and justified (4:58-5:18); FABRIK code shown without walking it (3:38)
principles.3: not-observed: no interface habit teaching; it is a devlog
principles.4: contradicted: hands straight to algorithm and code (bones, passes) with no analogy
principles.5: partly: chain, target, drag it around in the editor shows the algorithm literally (3:38)
principles.6: partly: rope built from the simplest primitives; no brute-force-first sequence beyond failed FABRIK reuse
principles.7: partly: relaxation insight (6:14-6:29) is told, not discovered, though the jitter wave and randomised order are told as findings
principles.8: not-observed: devlog pacing is driven by project order; idea rate drops (many sentences per small tweak) when he is showing code he cannot explain
principles.9: confirmed: same Point/Stick idea reused for rope (5:00), cable (7:13), cloth (7:49)
principles.10: confirmed: rope to complex test (6:52) to cloth grid (7:49); 500k then 1M particles (9:14-9:52)
principles.11: partly: Point, Stick, per-frame update, constraint, repeat is in dependency order; broader video order is chronological
principles.12: confirmed: ties to his old spider-leg project (2:41), a rope series he watched (4:43), GPT-3, Fiverr
principles.13: partly: plain language and real code; reasons are given for instancing (9:52) but not for FABRIK or Verlet math

new_moves.name: reuse-failure-as-motivation
new_moves.what: Apply the known technique to a new case, show it failing, then introduce the better tool
new_moves.evidence: 4:14-4:58 cable with FABRIK looks bad, then Point/Stick

new_moves.name: same-primitive-new-domain
new_moves.what: One small abstraction stretched across rope, cable, cloth to show its generality

new_moves.name: admit-skipping-the-hard-part
new_moves.what: Says plainly where he used a built-in or skipped collisions, which lowers the bar for the learner
new_moves.evidence: 8:39 ships built-in cloth; 7:13 no wall collision

new_moves.name: fix-by-iteration-not-cleverness
new_moves.what: Local fixes break neighbours, so just repeat the constraint pass

theory: This is a progress-diary, not a lecture, and its pedagogy lives in honest friction: shows the failing first try, the cheat, and the skipped hard part. The one real teaching sequence (Point, Stick, per-frame update, repeat until settled) works because the whole algorithm is tiny and then immediately re-used on cloth, so generality is shown not claimed.
velocity: Orchestrator: offer a 'try the old tool, watch it fail, then introduce the new one' playbook
Scene builder: keep one primitive on screen and swap the scenario (rope, cloth) rather than new scenes
Voice: include honest 'I skipped X because...' lines to mark what is out of scope
Evals: flag explanations that jump to code with no analogy or brute-force lead-in (FABRIK 2:59)
Learner model: record when the learner has seen the primitive in one domain so transfer examples can be chosen
quote: run these constraints a bunch of times to let it settle
